summary: Washburn Mountain's Aermotor fire tower, first raised on Alander Mountain in 1928, moved to Beebe Hill in the 1960s; Wikipedia calls the Beebe Hill tower defunct and unsafe.

facts.status_note: Left the Washburn Mountain site in 1963-64; the tower now stands on Beebe Hill, defunct and deemed unsafe per Wikipedia
facts.agency: Taconic State Park Commission, later NY Forest Fire Control

events.note: Erected on Alander Mountain, just over the Massachusetts line, by the Taconic State Park Commission
Tower dismantled after the area burned and the landowner asked for its removal; stored (location disputed)
Re-erected on Washburn Mountain; Wikipedia dates the rebuild to late 1932
Operation turned over to Forest Fire Control about 1935
Dismantled and carried by helicopter to Beebe Hill; Wikipedia gives 1964
Tower being set up atop Beebe Hill; a 1965 Berkshire Eagle item says construction was underway
Beebe Hill tower remained in operation until 1987
Local residents, the Forest Fire Lookout Association and DEC begin efforts to restore the tower
Washburn Mountain site registered with FFLOS on October 6, 2009 (US 545)
State forest website deemed the Beebe Hill tower unsafe as of late 2024

notes_for_editor: Unresolved, so not in facts: where the tower was stored 1930-33 (FFLOS says High Falls, Wikipedia says High Valley Farm); the move year to Beebe Hill (1963 FFLOS and Forest Lookouts, 1964 Wikipedia, 1965 Berkshire Eagle item says taken down the previous fall); Beebe Hill access (DEC page says a fire tower open to the public, Wikipedia says deemed unsafe late 2024), so access is unset. No source describes the Washburn Mountain site today. A search snippet from another site suggested operation ended 1988-89; not read, not used. The brief's note that the two Columbia/Telescope records share a register number was not checked. Confirm the Beebe Hill condition with DEC Region 4 before any visitor guidance.
